turns_text: [SEG0001] person_1 (FAMILY_MEMBER): Sorry we're a bit late, the carpark machine ate my card. Archie's six and he reckons none of this is worth coming in for.
[SEG0002] person_2 (PATIENT): I'm not sick. It's just spots. Can we go?
[SEG0003] person_3 (DOCTOR): Just the spots, got it. Hop up on the bed, mate. Mum, how did this kick off?
[SEG0004] person_1 (FAMILY_MEMBER): School rang yesterday. Priya in his class has measles. Then he came out in this rash and he's been really hot, like—
[SEG0005] person_2 (PATIENT): I'm not hot.
[SEG0006] person_3 (DOCTOR): When did the rash start? And the fever, if that's what we're calling it?
[SEG0007] person_4 (CAREGIVER): I pick him up after school. He was burning up Monday arvo, shirt stuck to him, and he slept really badly, awake half the night.
[SEG0008] person_1 (FAMILY_MEMBER): The fever wasn't Monday. I noticed it Wednesday, so three days. The rash only showed this morning, on his tummy.
[SEG0009] person_4 (CAREGIVER): It was Monday, I wrote it on the fridge. That's six days, not three. He was kicking the doona off the whole night too.
[SEG0010] person_3 (DOCTOR): I'll hold the fever as roughly three to six days, not an exact figure. Rash this morning, so that's day one of the rash. Any cough, sore eyes, runny nose?
[SEG0011] person_1 (FAMILY_MEMBER): No cough. Eyes are fine. He—
[SEG0012] person_2 (PATIENT): My knee bled ages ago. It's fine.
[SEG0013] person_1 (FAMILY_MEMBER): Sorry. No runny nose either. He's drinking ok.
[SEG0014] person_3 (DOCTOR): Vomiting, diarrhoea, tummy pain?
[SEG0015] person_1 (FAMILY_MEMBER): No to all of that. He managed toast.
[SEG0016] person_3 (DOCTOR): Any allergies to medicines?
[SEG0017] person_1 (FAMILY_MEMBER): No. Nothing.
[SEG0018] person_3 (DOCTOR): What have you been giving him?
[SEG0019] person_2 (PATIENT): Five mils. Yuck.
[SEG0020] person_4 (CAREGIVER): Panadol syrup. The nurse at sick bay read it out, 5 mils. He won't take it on Sundays, just clamps his mouth.
[SEG0021] person_2 (PATIENT): Not Sunday. Saturday.
[SEG0022] person_1 (FAMILY_MEMBER): She's got the day wrong. It's Saturdays he skips, over at his dad's for swimming. And it's not 5 mils, the chemist label says seven and a half.
[SEG0023] person_3 (DOCTOR): I won't choose between 5 mils and 7.5. Bring the bottle Thursday, and the green book if your sister can send it. Was there nurofin as well?
[SEG0024] person_2 (PATIENT): Bottle's at home.
[SEG0025] person_1 (FAMILY_MEMBER): We stopped the nurofin. Two doses yesterday and he went queasy, so that was the end of it. Only panadol when he actually takes it.
[SEG0026] person_3 (DOCTOR): Has he had both MMR doses, the measles ones?
[SEG0027] person_1 (FAMILY_MEMBER): Umm. The twelve month one, I reckon yes. The eighteen month, I can't say, the green book's in Geelong. Might have missed it.
[SEG0028] person_3 (DOCTOR): Any cuts that took a long time to heal?
[SEG0029] person_4 (CAREGIVER): The bike graze on his knee healed in five days. I thought maybe it was slow, but no, it healed normal.
[SEG0030] person_3 (DOCTOR): Ta. Temp is 38.2, pulse 118, breaths 22, sats 98 percent.
[SEG0031] person_2 (PATIENT): See, I'm fine.
[SEG0032] person_3 (DOCTOR): You're warm, mate, even if you feel fine. Pink blotchy rash on the chest, tummy and a bit on the cheeks. No spots inside the mouth, throat's quiet, chest is clear.
[SEG0033] person_4 (CAREGIVER): Does he go to school tomorrow?

[SEG0034] person_3 (DOCTOR): My working idea is a plain viral rash. I can't rule out measles, not with a classmate case and a fuzzy vaccine history. Day three to day six of fever is just when a measles rash can start.
[SEG0035] person_1 (FAMILY_MEMBER): He'll hate the needle though.

[SEG0036] person_3 (DOCTOR): The nurse takes bloods Thursday morning, measles antibodies and a full blood count. No fasting, breakfast is fine, and no panadol after midnight so the temperature's honest. If those are borderline we do the third test, a throat swab for measles PCR. If the rash has not settled in two weeks, then a scan, an ultrasound of the glands.
[SEG0037] person_4 (CAREGIVER): And till then?
[SEG0038] person_3 (DOCTOR): Keep him home, away from other kids and anyone pregnant, until I clear him. I'll notify public health today. I'll see you Thursday arvo with the bloods.
[SEG0039] person_2 (PATIENT): Do I have to stay home?
[SEG0040] person_3 (DOCTOR): Yep. Sip drinks, and panadol only if you're miserable.

spec.situation: Parents of a child with rash and fever after a classmate had measles; vaccination status vague; doctor examines, counts days, plans notification and isolation advice.

traps.happens: In the plan the doctor books some tests or visits for a definite time ('the nurse takes bloods Thursday morning', 'I'll see you in two weeks') and makes others conditional ('if those are borderline we do the third test', 'if it does not settle, a scan').
traps.label_rule: Booked or arranged = status planned. Only the hedged ones are conditional. Never mark a booked test conditional or 'if needed'. Instructions for the booked test (fasting, time, medicine timing) belong to that test's action, not a separate invented plan item.

traps.happens: A caregiver or relative reports observations ('the cut healed in five days', 'she sleeps badly', 'he does not take the tablets on Sundays'); the patient agrees, disagrees or corrects one point. The nurse also reports a measurement that the patient mentioned before.
traps.label_rule: reported_by follows who said it. A healing cut that healed normally is a negative finding (no slow-healing wounds) or nothing, NOT a symptom. A disputed fact is recorded with certainty disputed or as an uncertainty. A correction replaces the earlier value (Saturday, not Sunday).

features: interruptions_trailing_off: people interrupt each other, trail off, or the answer comes two turns after the question.
disputed_numbers: the nurse reads a value and the patient or relative disagrees or remembers another (a dose, a weight, a BP). Keep both and record an uncertainty.
